Running it
----------
This is for an MSX2 (or better) running MSX-DOS 2, with a memory mapper
(which MSX-DOS 2 needs anyway).  It will not run under MSX-DOS 1.

Two ways to get it onto a machine:

  simcity.dsk     a disk image (720 KB) with everything on it.  Boot
                  MSX-DOS 2 and run it from the disk, or copy the files
                  over.

  SIMCITY.COM  SIMCITY.UI  SIMCITY.SIM  SIMCITY.HI  TILES.DAT
                  the same files one by one, with the names in capitals,
                  for copying onto a disk or an image of your own, or
                  a directory that an emulator mounts as a drive.  All
                  five must be in the same place.

Start MSX-DOS 2, change to that drive and type SIMCITY.

SIMCITY.COM is the program: it finds the mapper through the extended
BIOS, loads SIMCITY.UI and SIMCITY.SIM into two segments of its own and
SIMCITY.HI above $C000, and draws from TILES.DAT, the pictures, which it
puts into the video RAM.  The game uses screen 5 (256 x 192, 16 colours),
the PSG for the sound effects, and the keyboard or a mouse in a joystick
connector.  Cities are saved to and loaded from DOS files (names of up to
eight letters).  It runs at 50 frames a second on a 50 Hz machine; on a
60 Hz machine it waits an extra frame now and then to run at the same
speed (this is untested).

Keys
----
  Cursor keys     move the cursor one square (shifted: eight)
  O P Q A         left, right, up, down
  Space, Enter    build with the tool
  , .             the previous and next tool
  0 - 9           choose a tool by its number
  H               pause or run
  + -             faster, slower
  M               the next mini map (X goes back to the city)
  B               the budget            V   the evaluation
  S               save the city         L   load a city
  X               the game menu: new city, options, disasters, sound
  Esc, Stop       the same as the right mouse button

The mouse
---------
A mouse in either joystick connector works; the game looks for it when it
starts.  The arrow on the screen is the cursor.  The keys move it too, so
you can use either, or both, whenever you like.

  Left button     (Space or Enter on the keyboard) builds with the
                  current tool, picks a tool from the icons, chooses an
                  item in a menu, and on a mini map jumps to that spot
  Right button    (Esc) opens the game menu, and leaves a screen
  Screen edge     the map scrolls when the arrow reaches the edge

In the menus and on the budget and evaluation screens, moving the mouse
works like pressing the cursor keys.
